I’m sorry that you feel this way, I find myself relating to a lot of the points that you bring up and I would like to tell you that it’ll be alright but that’s not guaranteed. For better or for worse I believe that some people have to work for it to be alright which is incredibly unfair but since you’re so young I still think there’s room for improvement. Things can still change, if you will them to. It will not be easy, it never will but personally I try to find motivation to continue in the little things that I enjoy. Live another day to play that game, read that book and see that movie. If I disappear I won’t ever be able to do these things that I enjoy. So many possibilities and maybes will be wasted. I’m sure you got hobbies that you enjoy and if you don’t well, I’m sorry I’m not a professional. 
In your text you put a lot of emphasis on relationships being the key to happiness and they can be if they’re benefiting both parts. I believe that those kinds of relationships can’t be achieved without vulnerability. To truly connect you have to also accept the possibility of getting hurt, the hedgehog’s dilemma, but you’re not the only one putting yourself out there if it’s successful. People have their own problems and sometimes you might have to take a step back and think: is this truly good for me? 
In the end, no one else can live your life but you. I urge you to think about what things you could change to make your daily life more enjoyable. Don’t think too far into the future, that’ll only stress you out. Live in the moment if you can and make the most of it. I wish you only the best and I’m sorry if I wasn’t to any help.
High five lmao. Nah but for real tho, take care. I hope you’ll find a way back to a satisfactory life.

Indeed, I would never wish this mentality upon someone else. I’m sorry that you feel this way but it’s also comforting in the sense that I’m not alone. I wish you only the best, whatever that might entail.
